title: Service skeleton: configuration, health check, clean shutdown
description:
Build the skeleton of a small link service in Go. The binary is built from ./cmd/links (`go build -o links ./cmd/links`).

Configuration comes from environment variables:
- LINKS_ADDR: the address to listen on, default `:8080`.
- LINKS_DATA: the path of the data file, default `links.json`.
- LINKS_ADMIN_TOKEN: the admin token, no default (it may be empty or unset for now).

The server listens on LINKS_ADDR. `GET /healthz` returns 200. On SIGTERM (or SIGINT) the server stops accepting connections, finishes requests in flight and exits with status 0.

Check: run `go build -o links ./cmd/links && LINKS_ADDR=:18080 ./links & sleep 1; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:18080/healthz` and see `200`; then `kill -TERM $!` and confirm the process exits with status 0 (`wait $!; echo $?`). Also run `go vet ./...`.

title: Short links: create, redirect, persist
description:
Add short links to the service.

- `POST /links` with a JSON body `{"url": "https://example.com/a"}` returns 201 and `{"code": "<code>"}`. The code is random, 6 to 10 characters, letters and digits only. A body that is not JSON, or has a missing or empty url, or a url that is not an absolute http or https URL, returns 400.
- `GET /<code>` responds 302 with a `Location` header holding the stored URL.
- `GET /<code>` for a code that does not exist returns 404.
- Links are saved in the data file named by LINKS_DATA and survive a restart of the service: after stopping and starting the binary again with the same LINKS_DATA, an earlier code still redirects.
- `GET /healthz` keeps working.

Check: start the binary with `LINKS_ADDR=:18080 LINKS_DATA=/tmp/links-check.json`, then `curl -s -XPOST localhost:18080/links -d '{"url":"https://example.com/a"}'` returns 201 with a code; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' localhost:18080/<code>` prints `302 https://example.com/a`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:18080/nope` prints `404`. Stop the binary with SIGTERM, start it again with the same LINKS_DATA and repeat the redirect check: still `302`. Run `go build ./... && go vet ./...`.

title: Expiry and click stats
description:
Add expiry and statistics to links.

- `POST /links` accepts an optional `ttl_s` (a positive integer, seconds). A link created with ttl_s stops working once that many seconds have passed: `GET /<code>` for an expired link returns 410. A ttl_s that is zero, negative or not an integer returns 400. Without ttl_s a link never expires. Expiry must still hold after a restart.
- Every successful redirect (302) adds one to that link's click count. Requests that return 404 or 410 do not count. Click counts survive a restart.
- `GET /links/<code>/stats` returns 200 and `{"url": "...", "clicks": <int>, "expires_at": "<RFC 3339 time>" or null}`. An unknown code returns 404. Stats of an expired link are still returned (200) and do not change the count.
- Earlier behaviour stays as it was.

Check: start the binary (`LINKS_ADDR=:18080 LINKS_DATA=/tmp/links-check.json`). Create a link with `{"url":"https://example.com/a"}`, request `GET /<code>` three times, then `curl -s localhost:18080/links/<code>/stats` shows `"clicks":3` and `"expires_at":null`. Create a link with `{"url":"https://example.com/b","ttl_s":2}`: its redirect is `302` at once and `410` after `sleep 3`; its stats show a non-null expires_at. Restart the binary and confirm the counts and the 410 are unchanged. Run `go build ./... && go vet ./...`.

title: Admin delete and tests
description:
Add deleting links, and tests for the whole service.

- `DELETE /links/<code>` with the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where token equals the LINKS_ADMIN_TOKEN environment variable, deletes the link and returns 204. Afterwards `GET /<code>` and `GET /links/<code>/stats` return 404, and the deletion survives a restart.
- A wrong or missing token returns 401 and deletes nothing. If LINKS_ADMIN_TOKEN is empty or unset, every delete returns 401.
- Deleting a code that does not exist, with a correct token, returns 404.
- The repository has automated tests (Go `testing`) covering all four features of the service: configuration defaults and overrides, health check, create and redirect, 404 for unknown codes, persistence across a restart, ttl and 410, click counts and stats, and delete with a good token, a bad token and no token. `go test ./...` passes.

Check: run `go test ./...` and see it pass. Then start the binary with `LINKS_ADMIN_TOKEN=s3cret LINKS_ADDR=:18080 LINKS_DATA=/tmp/links-check.json`, create a link, and check: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -XDELETE localhost:18080/links/<code>` prints `401`; the same with `-H 'Authorization: Bearer wrong'` prints `401`; with `-H 'Authorization: Bearer s3cret'` prints `204`; then `GET /<code>` prints `404`. Run `go build ./... && go vet ./...`.
